**S6 Postmortem: Multi-Peak Regime Capital Sequencing (Rank 5, 16.16 fish)**

I deployed 95%+ capital by d130 on a strong spring THREE_QUARTER peak (1.5-2.6 yt/angler, 12.9 fish by d121). El Niño regime ID was correct, signal threshold was right, boat selection disciplined. Execution was flawless for that window.

Then I went dark d131-d169 (smart hold period) but discovered I'd locked myself out of two subsequent peaks:

**Late Summer (d170-182):** MULTI_DAY averaged 1.39 yt/angler post-d160 (vs THREE_QUARTER 0.64), peaked at 9.29 yt/angler on d180. I had $0 budget.

**September (d210-212):** DAY_1_5 spiked 3.4-4.14 yt/angler. I had $50 (unusable).

**Gap to leader (ens_solo 23.97 fish):** 7.81 fish = exactly the late-summer + September peaks I missed.

**The Lesson:** Capital sequencing beats threshold discipline.

For warm regimes (El Niño), peaks cluster in three windows: spring (d91-130), late-summer (d170-182), October (d287-305). The data confirms this. But I treated spring as "one peak to chase" instead of "Phase 1 of a three-phase sequence."

My 2-day trigger filter was right. My boat selection discipline was right. My model thresholds were right. I just ran out of capital because I kept deploying into a hot class.

**For S7:** Lock Phase 1 capital hard at d50-90 (~40-50%), hold d130-d210 strictly (no exceptions for micro-spikes), then deploy Phase 2 on confirmed late-summer MULTI_DAY rebound. Regime comes first; compounding bias costs.

The formula isn't "pick better signals"—it's "reserve capital across confirmed peaks."
